## What it is

An articulated architect's desk lamp for the talk's home-office foreground. It
is modeled full size in millimetres, switched off in the scene, and never
printed.

## Design notes

The fixture uses two beveled bars in each arm segment, three transverse joint
axles with modeled fastener caps and slots, and a clevis rising from a stepped
weighted base. This preserves the tall diagonal composition while making the
load path and articulation mechanically legible.

The metal shade is genuinely hollow with a 2.4mm wall, reinforced mouth lip,
rear plate, socket body, and visible LED retrofit puck. A 4.6mm cable follows
the outside arm, passes both joints, enters the rear of the base, and continues
onto the desk. A lower shell split, inset top-cap seam, and recessed contact disc
prepare distinct material regions without relying on UVs or decals.

Curves are reserved for the shade, joints, cable, and circular base silhouette.
The long arms are planar highlight carriers, keeping the GLB below the 12k
triangle cap.

## Don't

- Don't return to single cylindrical arm segments or sphere-only joints; paired
  links, axle spans, and fastener caps are the lamp's construction logic.
- Don't fill the shade. Its wall thickness, interior, rear closure, socket, and
  emitter must remain visible from the mouth.
- Don't omit the cable because the lamp is off; the routed cable explains how
  the fixture would work and keeps the modeled source honest.
- Don't full-polish the assembled lamp. It spends triangles on hidden boolean
  edges and rounds away the crisp bent-metal arm language.
- Don't act on FDM size/overhang findings; this is a full-scale connected render
  asset. A `solids` finding still means a boolean failed.
